about: Commonwealth Fusion Systems is a Massachusetts-based fusion energy company spun out of MIT in 2018, based in Devens. It is building the SPARC tokamak using high-temperature superconducting magnets and plans the ARC power plant, with Google as a customer and Eni a major investor. It has raised roughly 3 billion dollars from investors including Bill Gates's Breakthrough Energy, Tiger Global and Google, making it among the best-funded fusion startups. Pre-revenue deep-tech with high profile in climate and technology media.

COX Group is a Spanish company headquartered in Seville that develops water, energy and infrastructure projects, including desalination, solar power plants and green hydrogen across Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America. Its business lines cover engineering, construction and operation of concessions, and it has raised large project financing. Privately held. B2B infrastructure developer with limited consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Crescent Energy is a Houston-based US independent oil and gas company listed on the NYSE (CRGY), formed in 2021 from KKR-backed Independence Energy and Contango. It owns producing assets in the Eagle Ford, Uinta, Permian, Rockies and Barnett basins, producing roughly 250,000 barrels of oil equivalent daily, and grows through acquisitions, including Vital Energy in 2025. Revenue is oil and gas sales. B2B upstream operator with no public consumer brand.

Cypress Creek Energy is an independent power producer and solar developer based in Durham, North Carolina, previously known as Cypress Creek Renewables. It develops, finances, builds and operates utility-scale solar and energy storage projects across the US, selling power to utilities and corporate buyers under long-term contracts. Founded in 2012, it is backed by private equity firms and lenders. B2B energy developer with little public awareness.

about: Diamondback Energy is an independent oil and natural gas producer based in Midland, Texas, listed on Nasdaq (FANG) and focused on the Permian Basin. It produces around 900,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day after acquiring Endeavor in 2024, and holds mineral interests through subsidiary Viper Energy. Sells to refiners and marketers; revenue exceeds 10 billion dollars. Founded 2007. B2B upstream operator with no consumer brand recognition.

Doral Renewables is a US developer, owner and operator of large-scale solar and wind projects, headquartered in Philadelphia and part of the Doral Group with Israeli parent origins. It builds utility-scale solar projects in the US, selling power to utilities and corporate offtakers, and has raised project financing from banks and tax equity investors. B2B renewable energy developer with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

DTE Energy is a Detroit-based diversified energy company listed on the NYSE (DTE). Its DTE Electric and DTE Gas utilities serve about 2.3 million electric and 1.3 million gas customers in Michigan, with additional businesses in renewable energy, energy trading and pipelines. Annual revenue is around 13 billion dollars, mostly regulated utility rates paid by households and businesses. Its Detroit Edison utility dates back to the 1890s. Well-known regional utility brand in Michigan with local sponsorships.

Duke Energy is one of the largest US electric utilities, headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, and listed on the NYSE (DUK). It supplies electricity to about 8.6 million customers and natural gas to over 1.7 million across the Carolinas, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, with fleet capacity of roughly 54,000 megawatts. Revenue is about 30 billion dollars from regulated rates. Founded in 1904. Well-known regional utility with local sports and community sponsorships.

EDF Power Solutions, formerly EDF Renewables North America, is the North American renewables arm of French state-owned EDF, based in San Diego, California. It develops, builds, owns and operates wind, solar and storage projects, with over 20 gigawatts developed in the US, Canada and Mexico, and provides asset management and O&M services. Customers are utilities and corporate offtakers. Rebranded as EDF power solutions in 2023. B2B energy developer, brand tied to the larger EDF group.

Emera is a Canadian energy and services company headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia, listed on the TSX (EMA). It owns regulated electric and gas utilities including Nova Scotia Power, Tampa Electric and Peoples Gas in Florida, New Mexico Gas, plus a stake in the Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, serving about 2.6 million customers. Annual revenue is around 7 billion Canadian dollars from regulated rates. Founded 1998. Regional utility brand with no strong global awareness.

EnBW (Energie Baden-Wurttemberg) is one of Germany's largest energy companies, headquartered in Karlsruhe and about 98 percent owned by the state of Baden-Wurttemberg and municipal associations. It generates, trades and distributes electricity, gas and water, operates grids, offshore wind farms and EV charging networks (EnBW mobility+), and serves millions of customers with about 27,000 employees and revenue over 40 billion euros. Founded 1997. Well-known German utility brand; local sports sponsor, including football.

Enfinity Global is a renewable energy developer and independent power producer with roots in Belgium and Italy, now headquartered in Miami, developing solar and storage projects across Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia-Pacific, and with a global project pipeline of several gigawatts. Backed by private equity and lenders, it sells power under long-term contracts to utilities and corporates. Founded in 2007. B2B energy developer with little public brand awareness.

about: Engie is a French multinational energy and services group headquartered in Paris (La Defense), listed on Euronext Paris (ENGI), with the French state as its largest shareholder. It generates and sells electricity, natural gas and renewable energy, operates networks and offers energy efficiency and building services, with about 97,000 employees and revenue around 70 billion euros, across Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and the US. Formed by the 2008 merger of Gaz de France and Suez. Strong consumer brand in France and Belgium and a sponsor of sport and events.

Entergy Corporation is an integrated electric utility holding company headquartered in New Orleans, listed on the NYSE (ETR). Its subsidiaries serve about 3 million customers in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas, and operate a sizeable nuclear fleet plus Entergy Wholesale Commodities. Revenue is around 12 billion dollars, mostly regulated rates. Founded in 1913. Well-known regional utility with community sponsorships rather than national consumer marketing.

Eos Energy Enterprises designs and manufactures zinc-based battery energy storage systems, with headquarters in Edison, New Jersey and a factory in Turtle Creek, Pennsylvania. Its Znyth aqueous zinc technology targets long-duration storage for utilities, renewable developers and commercial customers, with partners including Talen and Cerberus-linked financing. Listed on Nasdaq (EOSE), still early in revenue and loss-making. Founded 2008. B2B cleantech with limited consumer brand awareness.

Generate Capital is a San Francisco-based infrastructure investment and operating company founded in 2014 by Scott Jacobs, financing and owning sustainable infrastructure such as solar, battery storage, EV charging, waste-to-energy and water systems, then operating them under service contracts. Customers are corporations, municipalities and developers; it earns long-term service fees. Backed by Blackstone, Temasek, Goldman Sachs and others, with several billion dollars in capital. B2B climate infrastructure with low consumer visibility.

Greenko Group is one of India's largest renewable energy companies, headquartered in Hyderabad, with wind, solar, hydro and pumped-storage assets across several Indian states and a pipeline of integrated round-the-clock renewable projects. It sells power to state utilities and to commercial and industrial buyers under long-term contracts, and has been funded by investors including GIC, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Orix, with the founders' AM Green taking a larger role from 2024. Founded 2009. B2B power producer with limited public brand recognition.

Grenergy Renovables is a Spanish renewable energy developer and independent power producer headquartered in Madrid, listed on the Spanish stock exchange (GRE). It develops, builds and operates solar parks, wind and battery storage, with core markets in Spain, Chile, Mexico, Colombia, Italy and Germany and a pipeline of many gigawatts. Customers are utilities and corporate buyers; revenue comes from power sales and project sales. Founded 2007. B2B energy firm with little consumer awareness, though known in the Spanish stock market.

Hydro One is the largest electricity transmission and distribution utility in Ontario, Canada, headquartered in Toronto and listed on the TSX (H). It owns and operates about 30,000 km of high-voltage transmission lines and distributes power to around 1.5 million mostly rural customers. Revenue is regulated rates, roughly 8 billion Canadian dollars. The Province of Ontario retains a minority stake after partial privatisation in 2015. Well-known provincial utility, local community sponsorships only.

Hydro-Quebec is the state-owned electric utility of Quebec, Canada, headquartered in Montreal and owned by the Government of Quebec. It generates mostly hydroelectric power from dozens of dams, exports electricity to the US northeast and Ontario, and serves about 4.5 million customers in Quebec. Revenue is roughly 17 billion Canadian dollars annually. Founded 1944. Among the world's largest hydroelectric producers and a major corporate brand in Quebec, with a presence in arts and sports sponsorship.

IPX Power is a US power producing company based in Beaverton, Oregon, operating in clean energy and energy storage with a focus on developing and operating renewable generation projects. It sells electricity to utilities and other offtakers, and is privately held. Scale and project list are not confirmed from the input. B2B energy firm with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Masdar (Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company) is a state-owned renewable energy company headquartered in Abu Dhabi, owned by TAQA, Mubadala and ADNOC. It develops and operates solar, wind and green hydrogen projects in over 40 countries, targeting 100 GW of capacity by 2030, and runs Masdar City, a sustainability-focused urban development. Customers are utilities and governments. Founded 2006 and a host of the COP28 climate talks in Dubai in 2023. B2B with strong government and sustainability brand profile.

Matrix Renewables is a renewable energy platform headquartered in Madrid, owned by institutional investors, developing solar and storage projects in the US, Spain, Chile, Mexico, Colombia and Peru. It sells power to utilities under long-term contracts and has secured large project financing. B2B energy developer with limited consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Nexamp is a Boston-based developer, owner and operator of distributed solar and battery storage projects, focused on community solar and commercial rooftops in the US Northeast and Midwest. Founded in 2007 and later backed by Blackstone and Brookfield infrastructure investors, it sells clean power to utilities, businesses and subscribers who receive bill credits. Dozens of projects totalling more than a gigawatt. Customer-facing brand in community solar states, with low national awareness.

NextEra Energy is a major US energy company based in Juno Beach/Palm Beach, Florida and listed on the NYSE (NEE). Its regulated utility Florida Power & Light serves around 6 million customer accounts, while NextEra Energy Resources is the world's largest generator of wind and solar power, with large battery storage and nuclear operations. Revenue is roughly 25 billion dollars. Customers are households, utilities and corporate buyers. Founded in 1925. Strong utility brand in Florida; sponsors sports and community events there.

NiSource is a US regulated utility holding company headquartered in Merrillville, Indiana and listed on the NYSE (NI). Through NIPSCO and Columbia Gas companies it delivers natural gas and electricity to about 4 million customers in Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Kentucky and Maryland, with annual revenue near 5.5 billion dollars. It also invests in renewable generation. Founded 1912. Regional utility brand with local sponsorships only.

Ontario Power Generation (OPG) is the Ontario provincial government-owned electricity generator, headquartered in Toronto. It operates nuclear stations (Darlington and Pickering), large hydroelectric plants including Niagara Falls, and biomass and solar, producing roughly half of Ontario's electricity, and is developing small modular reactors at Darlington. Revenue is regulated and contract prices, about 7 billion Canadian dollars. Created from Ontario Hydro in 1999. Strong provincial brand, mainly public sector with local community sponsorships.

Origis Energy is a Miami-based developer and independent power producer of utility-scale solar and battery storage, with more than 20 GW of pipeline and operating projects across the United States, and a presence in Europe and Latin America. Founded 2011 by Johan Vanhee and Frank Hoynck, it sells power to utilities and corporates under long-term contracts. Backed by Antin Infrastructure Partners; the founder-led team has raised billions in project finance. B2B energy brand with little consumer awareness.

Peabody Energy is the largest private-sector coal producer in the United States, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri and listed on the NYSE (BTU). It mines thermal coal for power utilities and metallurgical coal for steelmakers at operations in the US and Australia, with annual revenue near 4 billion dollars. Founded 1883. Customers are power generators and steel manufacturers. B2B mining company with limited public recognition outside the energy and mining industries.

Recurrent Energy is the US-based solar and storage developer owned by Canadian Solar, headquartered in Austin, Texas after relocating from San Francisco. It develops, owns and operates utility-scale solar and battery projects, with a global pipeline of tens of gigawatts and operations in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific. Customers are utilities and corporate buyers under power purchase agreements. Founded 2006; Canadian Solar acquired the business in 2015. B2B energy developer, brand tied to its parent.

Rowan Digital Infrastructure is a Denver-based developer and operator of hyperscale and AI data centre campuses, seeking low-cost, renewable-powered capacity in the US. It builds large-scale facilities for cloud and AI tenants, aiming for industrial campuses with on-site power. Private and backed by institutional investors. B2B infrastructure company with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: RTE (Reseau de Transport d'Electricite) is France's electricity transmission system operator, headquartered in La Defense near Paris and owned by EDF (50.1 percent), CDC and CNP Assurances. It runs about 105,000 km of high-voltage lines, balances supply and demand and manages cross-border interconnections, with roughly 9,000 employees and revenue around 6 billion euros from regulated tariffs. Created 2000. Critical-infrastructure B2B brand known to the French public through Ecowatt alerts, but not a consumer marketer.

RWE is a German energy company headquartered in Essen, listed on the Frankfurt exchange (RWE) and a DAX member. It generates power from offshore and onshore wind, solar, hydro, gas and battery storage, is one of the world's largest offshore wind operators, and trades energy; the coal and nuclear exit is under way. Employs about 20,000 people, with revenue around 25 billion euros. Founded 1898. Customers are utilities and industry; consumer retail now largely handled elsewhere. Well-known German brand with football sponsorship history, including Bundesliga links.

SB Energy is a US renewable energy developer and operator owned by SoftBank Group, headquartered in San Francisco. It develops large solar and battery storage projects across the US, particularly Texas, and was part of OpenAI's Stargate data centre power effort. In 2025 it got a major investment linked to OpenAI. It sells power to utilities and corporates. Founded 2016 as SoftBank Energy. B2B energy business with limited consumer visibility but a high-profile parent.

Solaris Energy Infrastructure, formerly Solaris Oilfield Infrastructure, is a Houston-based company listed on the NYSE (SEI) that began with mobile proppant management systems for US shale drillers and now provides mobile gas-fired power generation for oil and gas operators and data centres, building a fleet of several hundred megawatts to over 1 GW. Customers are exploration and production companies and AI data centre developers; revenue is equipment rental and services. Founded 2014. B2B energy infrastructure with no consumer profile.

Sunrun is the largest US residential solar company, headquartered in San Francisco and listed on Nasdaq (RUN). It installs rooftop solar and home batteries, selling mainly through long-term leases and power purchase agreements, and serves over 1 million customers. Revenue is above 2 billion dollars, plus subscription income, and it also owns solar assets financed by investors. Founded 2007. Consumer-facing brand in states like California, Arizona and the Northeast, advertised via TV and partnerships.

Zenobe Energy is a UK-based developer and operator of grid-scale batteries and electric vehicle fleet charging and battery leasing, headquartered in London. It builds large battery storage sites for the electricity grid and finances electric bus depots and fleets for operators such as Transport for London bus operators. Founded 2017. Backed by institutional infrastructure investors. B2B energy storage company with limited consumer awareness but strong UK clean energy profile.

AESC (Envision AESC) is a Japanese-headquartered lithium-ion battery maker based in Yokohama, founded in 2007 as a Nissan and NEC joint venture and since 2018 owned by China's Envision Group. It produces cells and packs for electric vehicles, including the Nissan Leaf, at plants in Japan, the UK (Sunderland), the US (Tennessee, South Carolina) and China, with plans for more in France and Spain. Customers are automakers such as Nissan and Renault. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness.

Microvast is a US battery technology company headquartered in Stafford, Texas and listed on Nasdaq (MVST), designing and making lithium-ion battery cells, modules and packs with fast-charging chemistry for commercial and specialty vehicles, buses, trucks, rail and energy storage. It manufactures in Huzhou, China and in Clarksville, Tennessee, and had to restructure after a 2020 SPAC listing. Customers are commercial vehicle makers and fleets. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Alpha Generation is a US independent power producer based in Houston, Texas, that owns and operates natural gas-fired power plants. It sells power into wholesale markets. Crunchbase shows about $5.95 billion in funding, probably debt financing. Private. B2B energy company with little public brand awareness.

about: Capital Power is a North American power producer based in Edmonton, Alberta, owning natural gas, wind, solar, coal-to-gas and battery assets in Canada and the US with around 8 gigawatts of capacity, selling power into markets and under contracts. Customers are utilities, industrial buyers and wholesale markets. Spun out of EPCOR in 2009 and listed on the TSX (CPX). Funding shown reflects equity and debt raised. B2B energy producer, low consumer awareness beyond Alberta.

Darling Ingredients is a global converter of food waste and animal by-products into ingredients: fats, proteins, collagen and gelatin (Rousselot, Gelnex), pet food ingredients, and renewable fuels such as renewable diesel through the Diamond Green Diesel joint venture with Valero. Customers are food, feed, pharma, pet food and fuel markets. Headquartered in Irving, Texas, with over 260 plants on five continents and revenue around $6 billion. Listed on NYSE (DAR). B2B, little consumer awareness.

Duke Energy Florida is the regulated electric utility subsidiary of Duke Energy serving about 2 million customers across central and north Florida, including the St. Petersburg area, generating power from natural gas, nuclear, solar and other sources and delivering it to homes and businesses. Revenue comes from regulated rates. Crunchbase lists the Duke Energy parent location in Charlotte, North Carolina. Parent Duke Energy is listed on NYSE (DUK). Utility brand with local consumer familiarity, no consumer choice.

Enilive is the Eni subsidiary created in 2023 that combines Eni's retail fuel stations, biorefining, biofuels such as HVO, electric vehicle charging through Plenitude's charging business, car sharing (Enjoy), and lubricants. It operates thousands of stations in Italy and across Europe under the Eni brand. Headquartered in Rome, with KKR buying a 25 percent stake in 2024. Customers are drivers and businesses. Strong consumer brand in Italy and Europe, with a history in motorsport and sport sponsorship.

Octopus Energy is a UK energy retailer supplying electricity and gas to millions of households, known for smart tariffs, heat pumps and EV charging, and it also licenses the Kraken utility software platform to other energy suppliers worldwide. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, with operations in Europe, the US, Australia, Japan and elsewhere. Part of Octopus Group, with Kraken spun out as a separately funded business. Private. Strong consumer brand in the UK.

Santos is an Australian oil and gas company, founded in 1954 and headquartered in Adelaide, producing natural gas and LNG from the Cooper Basin, Queensland (GLNG), Papua New Guinea (PNG LNG), Darwin LNG and Bayu-Undan, with the Barossa project in development. Customers are utilities, LNG buyers in Asia and domestic gas users, with annual production of roughly 90 million barrels of oil equivalent. Listed on the ASX (STO). Known in Australia, with sports and community sponsorship.

Siemens Energy is a Munich-based energy technology group making gas and steam turbines, grid technologies, transformers, wind turbines through Siemens Gamesa, and electrolyzers and compressors. Customers are utilities, grid operators and industrial companies, with revenue about 35 to 40 billion euros and some 90,000 employees. Spun out of Siemens in 2020 and listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ENR). B2B brand, well known in industry and with the Siemens name carrying wider recognition.

Tabreed, the National Central Cooling Company, is a district cooling provider that produces and delivers chilled water to buildings in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and India, serving commercial, residential and public developments, with a sizeable capacity of over 1 million refrigeration tons. Headquartered in Abu Dhabi, with Mubadala and French utility Engie among its shareholders. Revenue comes from long-term capacity and consumption charges. Listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (TABREED). B2B, regional recognition.

Tata Power is one of India's largest integrated power companies, generating electricity from thermal, hydro, solar and wind, operating distribution utilities in Mumbai, Delhi and Odisha, and building rooftop solar, EV charging and solar manufacturing through Tata Power Solar. Customers are households, businesses and state utilities, with revenue above INR 60,000 crore. Part of the Tata Group, founded in 1919 and headquartered in Mumbai. Listed on the NSE and BSE (TATAPOWER). Strong consumer-facing brand in India.

Terna is the owner and operator of Italy's high-voltage electricity transmission grid, with about 75,000 kilometres of lines, and also manages dispatching and develops interconnections and storage projects. Customers are electricity generators, suppliers and consumers through regulated network tariffs. Headquartered in Rome. Listed on Borsa Italiana (TRN), with Cassa Depositi e Prestiti as a major shareholder. B2B, regulated utility with little consumer-facing brand.

Valero Energy is the world's largest independent petroleum refiner, with about 15 refineries making gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, plus renewable diesel through Diamond Green Diesel and ethanol plants. Sells fuel to wholesale customers and through branded retail stations, including Valero, Beacon and Shamrock, with revenue over $100 billion. Headquartered in San Antonio, Texas. Listed on NYSE (VLO). Recognised consumer fuel brand in the US, and a longtime motorsport and sports sponsor, including NASCAR and the Valero Texas Open.

XPLR Infrastructure, formerly NextEra Energy Partners, is a North Palm Beach, Florida company that owns contracted wind, solar and energy storage assets and natural gas pipelines, acquired from or developed with NextEra Energy. Customers are utilities and corporate offtakers under long-term power contracts. Renamed to XPLR in 2025 and listed on NYSE (XIFR), with NextEra Energy as its main sponsor and owner of a large stake. B2B yieldco, little public brand awareness.

AEP Transmission is the electric transmission business of American Electric Power, operating high-voltage lines and substations across Ohio, Indiana, Michigan, Texas, West Virginia and other states that form part of the PJM and ERCOT grids. Based in Columbus, Ohio, it earns regulated returns on its network assets. Customers are utilities and power generators, not consumers directly. Owned by AEP, listed on Nasdaq (AEP). B2B regulated infrastructure with low brand awareness.

about: Solid Power develops solid-state battery materials and cells for electric vehicles, including sulfide-based solid electrolytes, and partners with BMW, Ford and SK On for production lines and pilot cells. Headquartered in Louisville, Colorado, and founded in 2011. Revenue comes mainly from joint development agreements and electrolyte sales. Listed on Nasdaq (SLDP) after a 2021 SPAC merger with Decarbonization Plus Acquisition III. B2B technology supplier with little consumer awareness.

Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) is South Korea's state-controlled electric utility, which owns the national transmission and distribution network and a large share of generation through subsidiaries, selling electricity to households and industry, with nuclear and thermal plants and overseas projects including the UAE Barakah plant. Headquartered in Naju, with Seoul listed in the data. Listed on the Korea Exchange (015760) and NYSE (KEP), with the government as a major shareholder. Well-known domestic utility, but not consumer-choice.

Stegra, formerly H2 Green Steel, is a Stockholm-based company building a large green steel plant in Boden in northern Sweden that uses hydrogen from renewable power to produce near-zero-emission steel. Founded in 2020 by Harald Mix and Carl Hamilton. Customers include automakers such as Mercedes-Benz, Scania, and other manufacturers with offtake agreements. Crunchbase shows about $12.6 billion in funding including debt. Private, with construction ongoing and financing pressure reported in 2025. B2B brand with growing press attention.

Fortum is a Finnish clean energy company generating hydro, nuclear, wind and solar power, mainly in the Nordic countries and Poland, and selling electricity and heat to businesses, utilities and consumers, plus recycling and waste services. Headquartered in Espoo. Customers include industrial buyers and electricity wholesalers. Controlled by the Finnish state, which owns about 51 percent. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (FORTUM). Recognised energy brand in Finland.

LG Energy Solution is a South Korean maker of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles, energy storage systems and IT devices, supplying GM, Hyundai, Stellantis, Honda and other carmakers from plants in Korea, the US, Poland, China and Indonesia. Spun out of LG Chem in 2020 and listed on the Korea Exchange (373220) in January 2022, in one of the largest Korean IPOs. Headquartered in Seoul, with annual revenue of about 25 trillion won. B2B supplier, known through the LG brand.

Aditya Birla Renewables is the renewable energy arm of India's Aditya Birla Group, developing and operating solar and wind power plants and supplying clean electricity to industrial and commercial customers and utilities. Headquartered in Mumbai, with a portfolio of several gigawatts, and a target of over 10 gigawatts. Crunchbase shows about $2.1 billion in funding, including project financing. Part of the privately controlled Aditya Birla Group. B2B energy brand, though the Aditya Birla name is widely known in India.

Altus Power is a Stamford, Connecticut-based provider of commercial-scale solar power and energy storage, owning and operating rooftop and ground-mounted solar for commercial, industrial, public sector and community customers, and selling power under long-term contracts, plus EV charging. Revenue was about $200 million. It listed on NYSE (AMPS) via a 2021 SPAC merger, and agreed in 2025 to be acquired by TPG. B2B clean energy brand with little consumer awareness.

AMEA Power is a Dubai-based renewable energy developer and independent power producer building solar, wind and battery storage projects in Africa and the Middle East, including in Egypt, Morocco, Jordan, Zambia and South Africa. It sells electricity to national utilities and industrial customers under long-term contracts. Founded in 2016 by Hussain Al Nowais. Crunchbase shows about $2.1 billion in funding, including project debt. Privately held. B2B brand, no consumer awareness.

about: Base Power is an Austin, Texas startup that sells home battery systems and electricity plans to Texas homeowners, installing batteries at no upfront cost and aggregating them as a distributed power plant for the grid. Founded in 2023 by Zach Dell, Justin Lopas and others. Crunchbase shows about $2.3 billion in total funding after a $1 billion round in 2025. Private. Growing consumer brand in Texas, with a notable founder and investor profile.

BrightNight is a West Palm Beach, Florida renewable power developer that builds hybrid solar-plus-storage projects and sells clean power to utilities and large customers using its software platform for dispatchable renewable energy. Founded in 2018. Crunchbase shows about $2.4 billion in total funding, including project financing. Private. B2B energy brand with no consumer awareness.

about: Brookfield Renewable Partners is one of the world's largest publicly traded renewable power platforms, owning hydro, wind, solar and storage assets across North America, South America, Europe and Asia, and selling power to utilities and corporate buyers under long-term contracts. Part of Brookfield Asset Management, with offices in Toronto. Listed on NYSE (BEP) and TSX (BEP.UN). B2B energy brand, known in infrastructure investing with low consumer awareness.

Canadian Solar is a global solar and battery storage company that makes solar modules and e-STORAGE battery systems and develops utility-scale solar and storage projects, with manufacturing largely in China, Southeast Asia and the US. Founded in 2001 by Shawn Qu, with Canadian head office in Kitchener, Ontario. Customers are utilities, developers and distributors in dozens of countries. Listed on Nasdaq (CSIQ). B2B energy brand, known in the solar industry.

Centrus Energy supplies nuclear fuel and enrichment services, including low enriched uranium (LEU) for nuclear power plants and high-assay LEU (HALEU) for advanced reactors, working with the US Department of Energy at Piketon, Ohio. Headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland, and formerly part of USEC. Customers are utilities worldwide, with revenue of about $400 million. Listed on NYSE American (LEU). B2B nuclear fuel brand, notable in the energy sector.

Drax Group is a UK renewable energy company that generates power from biomass at the Drax Power Station in Selby, North Yorkshire, which provides about 5 percent of UK electricity, plus hydro and pumped storage, and produces wood pellets in North America. It also supplies electricity to businesses. Customers are the UK grid, industrial users and businesses. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (DRX). Well-known in UK energy, though also controversial over biomass.

Edify Energy is an Australian renewable energy developer based in Sydney, which develops, finances and operates utility-scale solar farms and battery storage in Australia. Revenue comes from power sales under long-term contracts with utilities and corporate buyers. Crunchbase shows about A$3.4 billion in total funding, mostly project finance. Privately held. B2B energy brand, with no consumer awareness.

about: Elia is the Belgian electricity transmission system operator, running Belgium's high-voltage grid and, through the Elia Group, also Germany's 50Hertz network, plus consulting and interconnector projects. Customers are electricity producers, suppliers and distributors via regulated tariffs. Headquartered in Brussels, with Belgian local authorities and Publi-T as the main shareholders and a free float. Listed on Euronext Brussels (ELI). Regulated infrastructure with no consumer-facing brand.

EnergyRe is a New York-based clean energy company, according to Crunchbase, which describes it as being at the center of the clean energy future and classifies it under energy. Crunchbase shows about $2.6 billion in total funding as listed, which may include project financing. Its projects, ownership and customers are not described in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Evergy is a Kansas City-based electric utility serving about 1.7 million customers in Kansas and Missouri, generating power from nuclear, coal, natural gas, wind and solar, and delivering it through regulated networks. Formed in 2018 by the merger of Westar Energy and Great Plains Energy. Revenue is around $5.5 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (EVRG). Local utility brand.

Fervo Energy is a geothermal company developing enhanced geothermal systems that use horizontal drilling from oil and gas techniques to produce round-the-clock clean power, with the Cape Station project in Utah and contracts with utilities and technology firms including Google. Founded in 2017 and based in Houston. Crunchbase shows about $1.9 billion in total funding. Private. Strong profile in the clean energy sector, with limited consumer awareness.

Fidra Energy is an Edinburgh, Scotland-based developer of large-scale battery energy storage, with its Thorpe Marsh project in Yorkshire of about 1.4 gigawatts among the largest in Europe. Revenue comes from grid services and energy trading. Crunchbase shows about 1.27 billion in funding, largely project finance. Privately held. B2B energy brand with no consumer awareness.

about: Form Energy develops iron-air batteries designed to store electricity for around 100 hours at low cost, for utilities and grid operators, with a factory in Weirton, West Virginia, and pilot projects with utilities such as Great River Energy and Xcel Energy. Headquartered in Somerville, Massachusetts, and founded in 2017. Crunchbase shows about $2.6 billion in total funding. Private. B2B technology brand known in energy storage, with little consumer awareness.

GE Vernova is a global energy equipment company spun out of General Electric in April 2024, making gas turbines, wind turbines, grid equipment and electrification software, and servicing power plants.
